subject: Migration crosswalk + proration playbook for entitlements
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@mediscribe.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Plan migration: mapping our current entitlements

Hi Nikhil / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the lower-latency routing and the dedicated cache behavior. Before we can sign anything, procurement and engineering need a clear mapping from our current SKU model to your modular tiering so we can estimate budget and regulatory audit traces.

High-level ask: can you produce a crosswalk that maps our existing entitlements (e.g., 100k tokens/month, 3 dedicated API keys, on-prem audit logs) into a recommended Redwood plan and note any feature gaps or overlap? We also need to understand:
- How proration works when seats / tokens are moved mid-cycle
- If feature-level entitlements (e.g., KV cache length, streaming concurrency) can be split across teams within a single contract

Procurement will also want a short migration timeline and any one-time credits you offer for migration complexity. Can you put something together by next week?

Thanks,
Marta
Head of Platform, Mediscribe

Attachment: current-entitlements-2027Q1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@mediscribe.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Plan migration: mapping our current entitlements

Thanks Marta — looping in Karthik from Solutions so we can capture the technical constraints. Per your ask, we prepared an initial crosswalk and a pragmatic migration playbook. Attached: migration-matrix.csv (mapping + notes) and a short amendment template. High level summary below.

Summary (TL;DR)
- Recommended target: Dedicated Plus (reserved capacity) with an add-on for private audit retention. This preserves your on-prem audit requirements while giving predictable throughput.
- Entitlement crosswalk: we map your 100k token baseline to a 120k committed token band (safety margin), 3 API keys -> 3 service identities, and on-prem audit logs -> Private (VPC) + extended retention add-on. Details in the CSV.
- Feature gating: streaming concurrency and KV cache length can be controlled per route via the Console. You can assign route-level overrides to particular service identities to simulate per-team entitlements.

Proration and credits
- Mid-cycle upgrades: we prorate unused committed tokens and apply them as credit toward the new band (standard one-line proration, no float).
- Downgrades: allowed at month boundary with a 30-day notice; any over-commitment in the prior period is billed and cannot be refunded but can be used as future credit if you purchase an over-time migration bundle.
- Migration credit: we can offer a one-time migration credit equal to 10% of the first 3 months' committed spend to offset onboarding work (subject to signature on amendment).

Proposed next steps (suggested timeline)
1) Review the attached matrix and flag any feature gaps (2 business days)
2) Agree on target band and migration credit (3 business days)
3) Sign amendment & schedule data-export run + route-level rollout (2 weeks)

Attachments: migration-matrix.csv (contains row-level mapping and action items), proposed-amendment_v1.pdf (pricing + credit line)

Let us know if you want a short video walkthrough — happy to run one with your infra folks.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0187
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@mediscribe.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@mediscribe.com
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Plan migration: mapping our current entitlements

Nikhil — thanks for the fast turnaround and the CSV. A few clarifications from Procurement & Engineering:

Procurement questions:
- Does the 10% migration credit stack with any volume-based promo you run? We may have an end-of-quarter co-term incentive.
- We need explicit wording in the amendment for audit-data residency and a sample SOC 2 evidence export process.

Engineering asks:
- Can we stage the migration per product line? We want to move 'Transcribe' first, then 'Summarize' three weeks later. Will token/proration handling work at a route level?
- Are there any latencies introduced by enabling the private retention add-on?

Also — we have a procurement freeze on new vendor FTE credits; any onboarding work should be covered by your migration credit rather than additional SOWs.

If you can confirm the credit stacking policy and update the amendment to include the residency + SOC 2 export steps, we can route to legal.

Thanks,
Marta
From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@mediscribe.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Plan migration: mapping our current entitlements

Marta — quick answers and a proposed redline approach so Procurement can move fast. See inline below and the updated amendment link.

On credit stacking: the migration credit (10%) is combinable with volume promos but not with administrative sign-up discounts. We'll call it out in the amendment: "migration_credit applies in conjunction with volume discounts but not cumulative sign-up promotions."

On residency & SOC 2 export: we added a short exhibit in the amendment that:
- Specifies audit log retention location (your VPC region)
- Outlines the SOC 2 evidence export steps (we'll produce an export bundle: logs, access traces, and KMS audit metadata; SIEM-friendly CSVs) and a 5-business-day SLA for ad-hoc export requests during the first 90 days.

Staged migration & route-level proration: yes — you can do staged migrations per route. Implementation notes:
- Token bands are committed at the contract level, but we track route-level consumption for internal accounting. During a staged migration, we prorate based on route-level consumption and apply credits to the global committed balance.
- Practically: move Transcribe first; we suggest a 14-day canary with traffic split 20/80 (new/old) then 50/50, then cutover. Our Console provides route traffic split and rollback in one click.

On latency for retention add-on: the retention add-on writes an additional async copy to your VPC object store; this adds negligible synchronous latency (sub-10ms on average); we measured +6ms median across similar customers.

Next steps we propose:
- I will update the amendment to include the exhibit and remove any language that implies stacking with sign-up promos (attached link).
- If Procurement signs off, we can issue the amendment and trigger a one-week migration window where our Solutions Eng team runs the CSV crosswalk and the on-call export test.

Doc links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/DEAL-2027-MED-481, DocuSign: https://na1.docusign.net/initialize?envelopeId=ABCD-1234-2027

Can we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow for final sign-off? I can invite Lauren and Karthik.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-amendment_v1.pdf (amendment stub)
